messages.content: 一位化學家正在進行一個實驗，使用一個2公斤的特定物質A樣本。實驗開始時，該物質的初始溫度為攝氏25度。然後，化學家將物質加熱到最終溫度攝氏75度。該實驗在1大氣壓力下進行。化學家重複進行相同物質的實驗，但這次的初始溫度為攝氏10度，最終溫度為攝氏50度。你能計算出在這兩個實驗的設定初始和最終條件下，物質的熵變化嗎？

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.content:
**Entropy change (ΔS)**  
For a material whose specific‑heat capacity \(c_{p}\) is approximately constant over the temperature range considered, the reversible entropy change when it is heated from an initial temperature \(T_{\text{i}}\) to a final temperature \(T_{\text{f}}\) at constant pressure is  

\[
\Delta S \;=\; m\,c_{p}\,\ln\!\left(\frac{T_{\text{f}}}{T_{\text{i}}}\right)
\]

where  
- \(m\) is the mass of the sample (kg),  
- \(c_{p}\) is the molar or mass specific heat capacity (kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹),  
- \(T_{\text{i}}\) and \(T_{\text{f}}\) are expressed in kelvin (K).

---

### 1. First experiment  
| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Mass \(m\) | 2 kg |
| Initial temperature \(T_{\text{i}}\) | 25 °C = 298 K |
| Final temperature \(T_{\text{f}}\) | 75 °C = 348 K |
| Pressure | 1 atm (constant, so no \(P\) term appears in the integral) |

Assuming a typical specific‑heat capacity for many solids/liquids of about \(c_{p}=1\;\text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\) (you should replace this with the actual value for substance A if known):

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta S_1 &= 2\;\text{kg}\times 1\;\frac{\text{kJ}}{\text{kg·K}}
            \times \ln\!\left(\frac{348}{298}\right)\\[4pt]
          &= 2\times \ln(1.1689)\;\text{kJ K}^{-1}\\[4pt]
          &\approx 2\times 0.1565\;\text{kJ K}^{-1}\\[4pt]
          &\approx 0.313\;\text{kJ K}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]

So the entropy increases by **≈ 0.31 kJ K⁻¹** during the first heating step.

---

### 2. Second experiment  
| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Mass \(m\) | 2 kg |
| Initial temperature \(T_{\text{i}}\) | 10 °C = 283 K |
| Final temperature \(T_{\text{f}}\) | 50 °C = 323 K |
| Pressure | 1 atm (constant) |

Using the same assumed \(c_{p}=1\;\text{kJ kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta S_2 &= 2\;\text{kg}\times 1\;\frac{\text{kJ}}{\text{kg·K}}
            \times \ln\!\left(\frac{323}{283}\right)\\[4pt]
          &= 2\times \ln(1.1417)\;\text{kJ K}^{-1}\\[4pt]
          &\approx 2\times 0.1325\;\text{kJ K}^{-1}\\[4pt]
          &\approx 0.265\;\text{kJ K}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence the entropy rises by **≈ 0.27 kJ K⁻¹** in the second experiment.

---

#### What you need to refine the numbers

The key missing piece is the exact specific‑heat capacity \(c_{p}\) of substance A over the temperature ranges 25–75 °C and 10–50 °C. If you have that data (either as a constant value or as a temperature‑dependent function), simply substitute it into the formula above. The pressure being constant means it does not appear explicitly in the entropy change calculation for a closed system undergoing only a temperature change at constant pressure.
